name: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
description: Thomas S. Kuhn's account of normal science, anomalies, and paradigm shifts — the work that moved 'paradigm' into general circulation and reframed scientific change as revolutionary rather than cumulative.

events.event: Published by the University of Chicago Press

relationships.description: Engages Popper's falsificationism as the dominant account of scientific method that the historical record challenges.

references.title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions — Wikipedia

name: The Logic of Scientific Discovery
description: Karl Popper's systematic statement of falsifiability as the demarcation criterion between science and non-science, first published in English translation of his Logik der Forschung (1934).

events.event: First English edition published by Hutchinson

references.title: The Logic of Scientific Discovery — Wikipedia

name: Science in Action
description: Bruno Latour's field guide to following scientists and engineers through society — a programmatic statement of laboratory studies and the anatomy of scientific 'facts in the making'.

relationships.description: Science and technology studies takes Kuhn's historicized account of science as a point of departure and moves it into ethnographic detail.

name: On the Origin of Species
description: Charles Darwin's presentation of descent with modification and natural selection — the foundational synthesis of evolutionary biology.

references.title: On the Origin of Species — Wikipedia

name: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
description: Isaac Newton's statement of the laws of motion and universal gravitation — the charter document of mathematical physics.

references.title: Principia — Wikipedia
references.description: Contents and editions of the Principia.

name: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
description: Claude Shannon's founding paper of information theory — entropy as a measure of information, channel capacity, and the separation of source and channel coding.

events.event: Published in two parts in the Bell System Technical Journal

references.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication — DOI record
references.description: Canonical record of the two-part paper.

name: On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies
description: Albert Einstein's special relativity paper — the two postulates from which the Lorentz transformations, relativity of simultaneity, and the invariance of the speed of light follow.

relationships.description: Generalizes and corrects Newtonian mechanics: inertial-frame relativity holds, but with the speed of light invariant rather than absolute time shared.

references.title: Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper — DOI record
references.description: Canonical record of the special relativity paper.

name: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids
description: Watson and Crick's one-page Nature communication of the B-form DNA double helix — the structural basis for genetic replication stated with 'novel features which are of considerable biological interest'.

references.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids — DOI record
references.description: Canonical record of the double-helix paper.

name: Experiments on Plant Hybridization
description: Gregor Mendel's pea-plant experiments establishing particulate inheritance — the segregation and independent assortment of traits, overlooked for a generation and then foundational to genetics.

events.event: Read to the Natural History Society of Brünn

relationships.description: Mendel read and annotated a copy of the Origin; his hybridization experiments respond to the open question of the mechanism of heredity.

specific.venue: Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn 4

references.title: MendelWeb
references.description: Electronic edition and apparatus for the 1866 paper.

name: GenBank
description: The NIH genetic sequence database — an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences, exchanged daily with the EMBL and DDBJ archives.

events.event: Established at Los Alamos National Laboratory; public releases begin

references.title: GenBank Overview
references.description: Scope, growth, and access to the archive.

name: Human Genome Project Reference Sequence
description: The finished euchromatic human genome reference sequence produced by the International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium — the anchor against which human genomic variation is still read.

relationships.description: Sequencing the human genome operationalizes the double-helix structure at whole-organism scale.

name: CERN Open Data Portal
description: CERN's public release of LHC collision datasets, simulated samples, and analysis software — the flagship open-data commitment of experimental particle physics.

events.event: Portal launched with first CMS open data releases

name: The Limits to Growth
description: The Club of Rome's World3 model report on population, industrial growth, pollution, food, and resource constraints — the twentieth century's most contested global-futures scenario study.

events.event: Presented at the Smithsonian; published by Universe Books

specific.venue: Universe Books (for the Club of Rome)

name: Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis (IPCC AR6 WG1)
description: Working Group I's contribution to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report — the consensus physical-science baseline on observed warming, attribution, and projected climate futures.

events.event: Approved line-by-line and released at IPCC-54

references.title: IPCC AR6 WG1 — DOI record
references.description: Canonical record of the assessment report.

name: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society (founding issue)
description: Henry Oldenburg's founding number of the Philosophical Transactions — the first journal dedicated to science, which established priority-of-publication and the scientific paper as an institution.

references.title: Philosophical Transactions — Wikipedia
references.description: History of the first scientific journal.
